history.summary: Legend: Lord Shiva served his devotee, the 14th-century Maithili poet-saint Vidyapati, disguised as a servant named Ugna; when they grew thirsty on the road, Shiva drew Ganga water from his matted locks. Vidyapati recognised the taste, fell at his feet, and Shiva revealed his true form, declaring he would remain there as a shivlinga. The present structure was built in 1932 and later renovated with a Yagnashala and Sanskarshala; a pond on the premises is said to be the one from which Shiva himself drank. Identity note: there are two Ugna Mahadev temples in Madhubani district — this file covers the well-known Bhawanipur temple (about 14 km from Madhubani), generally taken as the Vidyapati site; a second Ugna Mahadev Mandir stands at Bhairava Dham in Bisfi block. CSV town (Madhubani) corrected to Bhawanipur.

name: Ugna Mahadev Temple
town_description: Bhawanipur is a village in Madhubani district, Bihar, about 14 km from Madhubani town, known for the Ugna Mahadev temple linked to the poet Vidyapati. (CSV lists town as Madhubani — actual temple village is Bhawanipur.)

travel.road: About 14 km from Madhubani town; about 25 km from Darbhanga

visitor_information.best_time: Year-round; Savan and Mahashivratri for major festivals
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM – 9:00 PM (per travel guide; verify on arrival)
